title: ECAA: An affordance-aware comparative atlas of flexible cognition and species expertise
research_question: Which cognitive capacities are shared or independently evolved across nonhuman animals, how do ecological and social demands shape them, and how much transfers across tasks?
primary_hypothesis: A partially shared latent flexibility factor will coexist with strong domain-specific factors, and an affordance-aware mosaic model will predict held-out behavior better than a universal intelligence factor.

cohort_targets.note: planning targets, not observed enrollment; existing approved data may substitute

neural_measurements: existing approved MRI or diffusion MRI where validated

equations.item_response: logit(p_ikd) = alpha_kd + lambda_d theta_i + gamma_d E_i + delta_d S_i + rho_d M_ik + u_lab + u_i
equations.latent_trait: theta_i = mu_species(i) + beta1 Age_i + beta2 Rearing_i + beta3 SocialExposure_i + xi_i
equations.mosaic: z_i = Lambda theta_i + eta_i; Cov(eta_i) = Psi

falsification_rules: universal one-factor model matches mosaic model on held-out domains
affordance variables add no explanatory value
social learning does not alter later transfer
lack of measurement invariance across interfaces
ethics: no invasive neural manipulation required for core test
